target_customer: Engaged couples building wedding gift registries, with a take rate paid by retailers
problem: Couples had to register at several stores and guests did not know where to look; no registry combined independent retailers, big box stores and experiences.
business_model: Marketplace commission of 20 percent of each sale per VentureBeat

founders.name: Marika Chen
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and in VentureBeat.

founders.name: Sofia Chen
founders.background_notes: VentureBeat, August 2012, names sisters Marika and Sofia Chen as founders. The idea came when their elder sister got engaged.

exit.reason: No announcement found; CB Insights marks the company Dead and the cause is not public.

technical_complexity.rationale: Importing products from many retailers onto one registry and routing orders needed scraping or integrations plus a concierge service.

defensibility.rationale: Retailer relationships were a modest asset (98 percent of approached vendors agreed per VentureBeat) but registries were easy for larger players to match.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response is documented. Zola launched in 2013 with a similar universal pitch.

market_need_then: VentureBeat in August 2012 reported 3,000 brides signed up and 42 percent month on month growth, and the founders said registering across stores was laborious.

branding.domain_note: Used registrylove.com; it now redirects to chazofthedead.com, an unrelated site.

identity.logo: A logo file named registry-love appears in press but the design is not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and romantic, matched to the wedding audience

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch coverage exists. The name fit the category but no evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: RegistryLove presented at YC Demo Day in August 2012 with 3,000 brides and fast growth, but the directory lists it Inactive and CB Insights marks it dead. No post-mortem exists, so the cause is not public. Zola's 2013 launch shows well funded rivals entered the same universal registry space soon after.
notes: The $20K seed from Y Combinator in June 2012 rests on a single database (CB Insights) and likely reflects the standard YC deal; no press confirms it. Competitor search returned only current registry guides and 2013 Zola coverage, which is later than the batch, so the list is empty. A search snippet also named Jeremy Poteck as a third team member; not opened, so not recorded as a founder.
